Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 66, verse 1:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (1)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): O Prophet, who prohibited upon himself what Allah had made lawful for him, seeking by that the approval of his wives: why do you prohibit upon yourself the lawful that Allah has made lawful for you, seeking by your prohibition of it the approval of your wives?

The scholars differed concerning the lawful thing which Allah, mighty is His praise, had made lawful for His Messenger, and which he prohibited upon himself seeking the approval of his wives. Some of them said: it was Maria, his Coptic slave-girl. He prohibited her upon himself by an oath that he would not approach her, seeking thereby the pleasure of Hafsah bint Umar, his wife, because she had become jealous that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been alone with her on her day and in her apartment.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi related to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, saying: Abu Ghassan related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam related to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had relations with Umm Ibrahim in the house of one of his wives. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, in my house and on my bed?" So he made her forbidden to himself. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can you make forbidden to yourself what is lawful?" So he swore to her by Allah that he would not approach her. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives﴾. Zayd said: his saying "you are forbidden to me" is idle talk (laghw).

Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind related to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Masruq said: The Prophet (ﷺ) made his slave-girl forbidden, and took an oath concerning her, so he made the lawful forbidden. And regarding the oath, He said: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾.

Yunus ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made an oath of abstinence and made forbidden, so he was reproached for the prohibition, and he was commanded to expiate the oath.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that he said to her: "You are forbidden to me, and by Allah I will not approach you."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives﴾. He said: al-Sha'bi used to say: he forbade her to himself and swore he would not approach her, so he was reproached for the prohibition, and the expiation came for the oath.

Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and Amir al-Sha'bi, that the Prophet (ﷺ) made his slave-girl forbidden. al-Sha'bi said: he swore an oath along with the prohibition, so Allah reproached him for the prohibition and made for him the expiation of the oath.

Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾: a woman among the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his slave-girl in her house. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, how did this happen, and I was the least of them in your eyes?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Be silent, do not mention this to anyone; she is forbidden to me if I approach her after this, ever." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can you make forbidden to yourself what Allah has made lawful for you, when you say: she is forbidden to me forever?" He said: "By Allah, I will never come to her." So Allah said: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾ ... to the end of the verse. "I have forgiven you this, and your saying 'By Allah' ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths, and Allah is your Protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾."

It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a slave-girl, and he had relations with her. Hafsah saw him, and it was Aisha's day, and the two of them were allies against him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Keep this secret from me, and do not mention to Aisha what you have seen." Hafsah mentioned it to Aisha, and Aisha became angry, and she kept at the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) until he swore that he would never approach her. Then Allah revealed this verse, and commanded him to expiate his oath and to go to his slave-girl.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Amir, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾: concerning a slave-girl with whom he had relations, and Hafsah looked upon them, so he said: "She is forbidden to me; keep this hidden and do not tell anyone," but she mentioned it.

Others said: Rather, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made his slave-girl forbidden, so Allah, mighty and majestic, made his prohibition of her equivalent to an oath, and He obligated for it the expiation like what He obligated for an oath when its swearer breaks it.

Those who said this:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾: Allah commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers, when they prohibit something of what Allah has made lawful for them, to expiate their oaths by feeding ten needy persons, or clothing them, or freeing a slave; and that does not apply to divorce.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿and He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾. He said: Hafsah and Aisha were close friends, and they were two wives of the Prophet (ﷺ). Hafsah went to her father and spoke with him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for his slave-girl, and she remained with him in Hafsah's house, and it was the day on which he would come to Aisha. Hafsah returned and found them in her house, and she began waiting for her to leave, and she was greatly jealous. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) let his slave-girl out, and Hafsah entered and said: "I have seen who was with you. By Allah, you have done this to me." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I will satisfy you. I am going to tell you a secret, so guard it." She said: "What is it?" He said: "I call you to witness that this slave-girl of mine is forbidden to me, for your pleasure." Hafsah and Aisha were allies against the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), so Hafsah went to Aisha and confided to her: "Rejoice, the Prophet has made his slave-girl forbidden to himself." When the secret of the Prophet (ﷺ) was disclosed, Allah, mighty and majestic, made the Prophet (ﷺ) aware of it, and Allah revealed to His Messenger, because the two of them had allied against him: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿and He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾.

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, saying: Hisham al-Dastuwa'i related to us, saying: Yahya wrote to me, relating from Ya'la ibn Hakim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that Ibn Abbas used to say: "In the case of the prohibited (haram), there is an oath which one expiates." Ibn Abbas also said, regarding: ﴿There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example﴾, meaning that the Prophet (ﷺ) made his slave-girl forbidden, so Allah, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾. So he expiated his oath, and thus made the prohibition an oath.

Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, who said: Abu Uthman informed us that the Prophet (ﷺ) entered the house of Hafsah, and she was not there. His slave-girl came to him, and he drew a curtain over her. Hafsah came and sat at the door until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished his need. She said: "By Allah, you have done this to me; you had relations with her in my house," or words to that effect. He said: "And the Prophet (ﷺ) made her forbidden," or words to that effect.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾ ... the verse. He said: he made forbidden his Coptic slave-girl, the mother of his son Ibrahim, called Maria, on Hafsah's day, and he confided that to her, so Aisha found out, and they were allies against the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ). So Allah made lawful for him what he had forbidden to himself, and he was commanded to expiate his oath, and he was reproached for that, and he said: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths, and Allah is your Protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾. Qatadah said: al-Hasan used to say he made her forbidden to himself, so Allah placed in it the expiation of an oath.

Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) made her forbidden, meaning his slave-girl, and it became an oath.

Sa'id ibn Yahya related to us, saying: my father related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: Who were the two women? He said: Aisha and Hafsah. The beginning of the narration concerned Umm Ibrahim the Coptic, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had relations with in Hafsah's house on her day. Hafsah found him out and said: 'O Prophet of Allah, you have come to me with something you have not done with any of your wives, on my day, in my turn, and on my bed.' He said: 'Are you not pleased that I make her forbidden, so that I will not approach her?' She said: 'Yes.' So he made her forbidden, and said: 'Do not mention that to anyone.' She mentioned it to Aisha, and Allah, mighty and majestic, made it known to him, and Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives﴾ ... all the verses. It has reached us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) expiated his oath, and had relations with his slave-girl."

Others said: That was a drink which he used to drink, which pleased him.

Those who said this:

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu Dawud related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi, who said: This verse was revealed concerning a drink: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives﴾.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu Qatan al-Baghdadi, Amr ibn al-Haytham, related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, the same.

He said: Abu Qatan related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Ibrahim related to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: It was revealed concerning a drink.

The correct view on this matter is to say: what the Prophet (ﷺ) prohibited upon himself was something Allah had made lawful for him. It is possible that it was his slave-girl, it is possible that it was a drink of the drinks, and it is possible that it was something else. Whichever it was, it was the prohibition of a thing that was lawful for him, so Allah reproached him for prohibiting upon himself what He had made lawful for him, and explained to him the dissolution of his oath, in an oath he had sworn along with his prohibition of what he had forbidden to himself.

If someone says: What is your proof that he (ﷺ) swore an oath along with his prohibition of what he forbade? You know the saying of those who said that there was nothing from the Prophet (ﷺ) in that but the prohibition, and that the prohibition is the oath. It is said: The proof of this is clear: in no Arabic or non-Arabic language is it understood that the saying of one who says to his slave-girl, or to food or drink, "this is forbidden to me" is an oath. Since that is not understood, it is evident that an oath is other than a speaker's saying to a lawful thing: "it is forbidden to me." When that is so, what we said is correct and what contradicts it is invalid. Furthermore, it is possible that the Prophet's (ﷺ) prohibition of what he forbade upon himself from the lawful, which Allah, may He be exalted, had made lawful for him, was by an oath, so that His saying: ﴿Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful﴾ means: why do you swear not to approach the thing Allah has made lawful for you, thereby forbidding it to yourself by an oath.

We only said that the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade that and swore along with his prohibition, as:

Al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah related to me, saying: Maslamah ibn Alqamah related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made an oath of abstinence and made forbidden, so he was commanded in the oath of abstinence to expiate, and it was said to him concerning the prohibition: ﴿Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And Allah is Forgiving, O Muhammad, of the sins of the repentant of His servants, from their sins, and He has forgiven you your prohibition upon yourself of what Allah had made lawful for you. He is Merciful to His servants, not punishing them for sins they have repented of after repentance.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 66, verses 2–3:

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿Indeed, Allah has ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths. And Allah is your Protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾ (2):

His exalted remembrance says: Allah, mighty and majestic, has clarified for you the dissolution of your oaths and set its limits for you, O people. ﴿And Allah is your Protector﴾ — He will support you with His victory, O believers. ﴿And He is the Knowing﴾ of your interests, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His management of you and His directing you in what He knows best.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿And [recall] when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement. And when she informed [another] of it and Allah caused the Prophet to know of it, he made known [to her] part of it and ignored part. So when he informed her of it, she said, "Who told you this?" He said, "The Knowing, the Acquainted informed me"﴾ (3):

His exalted remembrance says: ﴿And [recall] when the Prophet﴾ — Muhammad ﷺ — ﴿confided to one of his wives﴾. She is, according to Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, Zayd ibn Aslam, his son 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, Hafsah. We have already mentioned the narration concerning this earlier.

* *

And His words: ﴿a statement﴾.

The statement he confided to her, according to these scholars, is his saying to the one of his wives to whom he confided it that he had forbidden his slave-girl (Mariyah), or that he had forbidden for himself what Allah, His praise be exalted, had made lawful for him, and his swearing an oath to that effect, and his saying, "Do not mention that to anyone."

* *

And His words: ﴿So when she informed [another] of it﴾.

His exalted remembrance says: when she informed her companion of the statement the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had confided to her, ﴿and Allah caused him to know of it﴾ — that is, Allah made His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ aware that she had informed her companion of that.

* *

And His words: ﴿he made known [to her] part of it and ignored part﴾.

The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the principal cities, other than al-Kisa'i, read ﴿عَرَّفَ﴾ with a shaddah on the ra', meaning: the Prophet ﷺ made Hafsah aware of part of that statement and informed her of it. Al-Kisa'i reported from al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and Qatadah that they read it ﴿عَرَفَ﴾ without a shaddah on the ra', meaning: he recognised for Hafsah part of that action she had done in disclosing his secret, which he had asked her to keep; that is, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was angered by that and repaid her for it. This comes from the saying of one who says to someone who has wronged him, "I will certainly make you know, O so-and-so, what you did," meaning, "I will certainly repay you for it." They said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ repaid her for that act by divorcing her.

The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who reads ﴿عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ﴾ with a shaddah on the ra', meaning: the Prophet ﷺ made Hafsah aware — that is, of what Allah made him know of her informing her companion — because of the consensus of the authorities among the reciters upon it.

* *

And His words: ﴿and ignored part﴾.

He means: and he refrained from informing her of part of it.

Those who interpret the Qur'an said similarly to what we have said. Among those who said so:

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And [recall] when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement﴾ — his saying to her, "Do not mention it" — ﴿And when she informed [another] of it and Allah caused him to know of it, he made known [to her] part of it and ignored part﴾; and he was generous ﷺ.

* *

And His words: ﴿So when he informed her of it﴾.

He says: when the Prophet of Allah informed Hafsah of what Allah had made him know concerning her disclosure of the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to 'A'ishah, ﴿she said, "Who told you this?"﴾ — that is, Hafsah said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: who informed you of this news and told you of it? ﴿He said, "The Knowing, the Acquainted informed me"﴾ — His exalted remembrance says: the Prophet of Allah Muhammad said to Hafsah: the Knowing of His servants' secret inclinations and the innermost thoughts of their hearts, the Acquainted with their affairs, from whom nothing is hidden, informed me of it.

Those who interpret the Qur'an said similarly to what we have said. Among those who said so:

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿So when he informed her of it, she said, "Who told you this?"﴾ — and she had no doubt that her companion had informed on her — ﴿He said, "The Knowing, the Acquainted informed me."﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 66, verse 4:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have certainly inclined [to that], but if you cooperate against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous of the believers, and after that the angels are [his] supporters.﴾ (66:4)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: "If you two turn in repentance to Allah, O two women, then your hearts have inclined toward the love of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked, namely his abandoning his slave-girl and forbidding her to himself, or forbidding what had been lawful to him, which he had made unlawful for himself because of Hafsah."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the like of what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have certainly inclined﴾, he said: "It means: your hearts have deviated; it means: your hearts have sinned."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Talhah related to us, from Zubayd, from Mujahid, who said: "We used to think that His saying ﴿your hearts have inclined﴾ was a minor matter, until I heard the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have certainly deviated﴾ (zaghat)."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿your hearts have inclined﴾: i.e., your hearts have leaned.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿your hearts have inclined﴾: your hearts have leaned.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿your hearts have inclined﴾: "It means: they deviated."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿your hearts have inclined﴾, he said: "Your hearts have deviated."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have certainly inclined﴾, and he said: "It pleased them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ abandon his slave-girl, and this was agreeable to them. ﴿Your hearts have inclined﴾ means that what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked pleased them."

* *

His saying: ﴿but if you cooperate against him﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the one to whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ confided his speech, and the one to whom she divulged his speech, and they are 'A'ishah and Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with them both.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I was always eager to ask 'Umar about the two wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, of whom God, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have certainly inclined﴾. He said: So 'Umar performed the pilgrimage, and I performed it with him. When we were at some part of the road, 'Umar turned aside, and I turned aside with him carrying a water-skin. Then he came to me, and I poured water over his hand, and he performed ablution. I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two wives of the Prophet ﷺ to whom God said: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have certainly inclined﴾?' 'Umar said: 'How astonishing you are, O Ibn 'Abbas!'" Al-Zuhri said: "He disliked what he asked, and did not conceal it. He said: 'They are Hafsah and 'A'ishah.'" He then began to relate the narration, saying: "We, the company of Quraysh, used to dominate women. When we came to Madinah..." and he related the hadith in full.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Ashhab informed us, from Malik, from Abu al-Nadr, from 'Ali ibn Husayn, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, about the two women who cooperated against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "'A'ishah and Hafsah."

Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Ubayd ibn Hunayn, that he heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "I remained for a year wanting to ask 'Umar ibn al-Khattab about the two women who cooperated, but I could not find an opportunity to ask him, until he set out for the pilgrimage, and I accompanied him. When we reached Marr al-Zahran, he went to relieve himself and said: 'Catch up to me with a water-skin.' When he finished his need and returned, I brought him the water-skin and poured it over him, and I saw an opportunity, so I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two women who cooperated against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?' Before I had finished my speech, he said: ''A'ishah and Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with them both.'"

Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, both saying: 'Umar ibn Yunus related to us, saying: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar related to us, saying: Simak Abu Zumayl related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas related to me, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab related to me, saying: "When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ withdrew from his wives, I entered upon him, and I saw anger in his face. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what has troubled you concerning the matter of the women? If you have divorced them, then Allah is with you, and His angels, and Jibril and Mika'il, and I and Abu Bakr are with you.' I rarely spoke and praised Allah with speech except that I hoped Allah would confirm my words. Then this verse was revealed, the verse of choice: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾, and ﴿but if you cooperate against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous of the believers...﴾ to the end of the verse. 'A'ishah, daughter of Abu Bakr, and Hafsah used to cooperate against the rest of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ."

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿but if you cooperate against him﴾: "It means: against the disobedience of the Prophet ﷺ and his harming."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Ibn 'Abbas said to 'Umar: "O Commander of the Faithful, I want to ask you about a matter, and I am in awe of you." He said: "Do not be in awe of me." So he said: "Who are the two who cooperated against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "'A'ishah and Hafsah."

* *

His saying: ﴿then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous of the believers﴾

It means: indeed Allah is his guardian and helper, and the righteous of the believers, and the best of the believers too, are his protector and helper.

It has been said that by "the righteous of the believers" in this place is meant Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Those who said that:

'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, he said: "Abu Bakr and 'Umar."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, he said: "The best of the believers are Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and 'Umar."

Ishaq ibn Isra'il related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa al-Sinani related to us — from a village in Marw called Sinan — from 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman, who said: "I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say regarding His saying: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾: Abu Bakr and 'Umar."

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾: "It means: the best of the believers."

Others said: by "the righteous of the believers" is meant the prophets, may God's blessings be upon them.

Those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, he said: "They are the prophets."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, he said: "They are the prophets."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, he said: "The prophets."

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that His saying: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, although it is in singular form, is meant in the sense of the plural. It is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. "Mankind" is in singular form but is meant in the sense of the plural. It is also like a man's saying: "Let no one recite to you except a reciter of the Qur'an." "A reciter of the Qur'an" is singular in form, but its meaning is plural, because he has permitted every reciter of the Qur'an to recite to him, whether one or many.

* *

His saying: ﴿and after that the angels are [his] supporters﴾

It means: the angels, along with Jibril and the righteous of the believers, are helpers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ against whoever harms him and intends to hurt him. "Supporters" (zahir) in this place is singular in form but plural in meaning. Had it been expressed in the plural form, it would have been said: "and the angels after that are supporters" (zuhara').

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿but if you cooperate against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous of the believers﴾: He began with the righteous of the believers here before the angels. He said: ﴿and the angels after that are supporters﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 66, verse 5:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you, submissive, faithful, obedient, penitent, worshipful, given to travel, previously married and virgins.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: It may be that the Lord of Muhammad, if he divorces you, O company of the wives of Muhammad ﷺ, will substitute for him wives better than you.

It has been said that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as a warning from Allah to his wives when they banded together against him in jealousy.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Humayd al-Tawil informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ banded together against him in jealousy, so I said to them: "It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you." He said: So it was revealed thus.

Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, from Umar, who said: It reached me concerning some of our mothers, the Mothers of the Believers, severity toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and their harming him, so I went around to them one by one, admonishing them and forbidding them from harming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I said: "If you refuse, Allah will substitute for him better than you," until I came to... I think he said Zaynab, and she said: "O son of al-Khattab, is there not in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what admonishes his wives, that you should admonish them?" So I held back, and Allah revealed: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you.﴾

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: Something reached me concerning the Mothers of the Believers, so I went around to them saying: "Either you desist from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or Allah will substitute for him wives better than you," until I came to one of the Mothers of the Believers, who said: "O Umar, is there not in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what admonishes his wives, that you should admonish them?" So I desisted, and Allah revealed: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you, submissive, faithful...﴾ to the end of the verse.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: ﴿an yubdilahu﴾. Some of the readers of Makkah, Madinah and Basra recited it with a doubled dal: "yubaddilahu azwajan" from tabdil (substitution with doubling of the second radical). The majority of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿yubdilahu﴾ with a single dal, from ibdal (substitution).

The correct view is that both are well-known recitations, sound in meaning, so whichever of them the reader recites is correct.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿muslimat﴾

He says: submissive to Allah in obedience. ﴿mu'minat﴾ means believing in Allah and His Messenger.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿qanitat﴾

He says: obedient to Allah.

As related:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding Allah's saying ﴿qanitat﴾: "obedient."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿qanitat﴾: "obedient."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿ta'ibat﴾

He says: returning to what Allah loves of obedience from them, turning away from what He dislikes from them. ﴿'abidat﴾ means humbling themselves before Allah through obedience to Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿sa'ihat﴾

He says: fasting.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿sa'ihat﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is fasting.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿sa'ihat﴾: "fasting."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿sa'ihat﴾: "fasting."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "al-sa'ihat" are "al-sa'imat" (the fasting women).

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿sa'ihat﴾: he means "fasting."

Others said: al-sa'ihat are the emigrants (al-muhajirat).

Mention of those who said that:

Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: "al-sa'ihat" are the emigrants.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿sa'ihat﴾: "emigrants. There is no travelling (siyahah) in the Qur'an or in the community of Muhammad except hijrah, and it is what Allah means by ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾."

We have already made clear the correct view concerning the meaning of al-sa'ihin earlier, with its evidences, along with mention of the differing opinions on it, and we disliked repeating it.

Some of the grammarians used to say: we see that the fasting person was only called sa'ih because the traveller (sa'ih) carries no provision, and eats wherever he finds food; so it seems to have been taken from that.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿thayyibat﴾

They are those whose virginity has been taken and whose maidenhead has gone. ﴿wa-abkaran﴾ are those who have not been co-habited with and whose virginity has not been taken.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 66, verse 6:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, harsh and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded.﴾

His, may He be remembered, saying: O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿protect yourselves﴾ means: teach some of you others what you should protect yourselves with from the Fire that you know of, and repel it from yourselves if you act upon it by obeying Allah. And act in obedience to Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿and your families, a Fire﴾

means: teach your families, through acting in obedience to Allah, what will protect them from the Fire.

Those of the interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from a man, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), concerning His saying: ﴿protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones﴾ he said: Teach them and discipline them.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from a man, from ʿAli: ﴿protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ he said: Discipline them, teach them.

⁕ al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahhan narrated to me, saying: Saʿid ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Dabbi, from al-Hakam, from ʿAli, the like of it.

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning his saying: ﴿protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ he said: Act in obedience to Allah, be wary of disobeying Allah, and command your families to remember Allah, and Allah will save you from the Fire.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ he said: Be wary of Allah, and enjoin your families to be wary of Allah.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones﴾ he said: [It means] that he protects them by commanding them to obey Allah and forbidding them from disobeying Him, and that he stands over them in the matter of Allah, commanding them to it and helping them with it; so when you see a disobedience to Allah, you restrain them from it and deter them from it.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ he said: Command them to obey Allah, and forbid them from disobeying Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿whose fuel is people﴾

means: its firewood, which is kindled under this Fire, are the children of Adam, and stones of sulphur.

* *

His saying: ﴿over which are angels, harsh and severe﴾

means: over this Fire are angels from among the angels of Allah, harsh toward the people of the Fire, severe against them. ﴿who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them﴾ means: they do not oppose Allah in His command that He orders them with. ﴿and do what they are commanded﴾ means: and they carry out what their Lord commands them.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have disbelieved, do not make excuses today; you are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾ [66:7].

Exalted is His remembrance, speaking of what He will say on the Day of Resurrection to those who denied His oneness in the world: ﴿O you who have disbelieved﴾ [in Allah], ﴿do not make excuses today; you are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾. He means: it will be said to them, "You are only being rewarded today, which is the Day of Resurrection, and you are being given the recompense for your deeds that you used to do in the world, so do not seek excuses for them."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 66, verse 8:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance (tawbatan nasuhan). Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and on their right. They will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent."﴾ (8)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: O you who have affirmed Allah (as true), ﴿repent to Allah﴾, meaning: return from your sins to the obedience of Allah and to what pleases Him concerning you, ﴿with sincere repentance﴾, meaning: a return in which you never revert, ever.

And in accordance with what we have said in the interpretation of His saying ﴿nasuhan﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said:

Mention of those who said that:

Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: Umar was asked about sincere repentance (al-tawba al-nasuh). He said: Sincere repentance is that a man repents from an evil deed and then never returns to it, ever.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from Umar, who said: Sincere repentance is that you repent from a sin and then do not return to it, or do not wish to return to it.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir delivering a sermon, saying: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, say: ﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance﴾ — he said: a person commits a sin and then does not return to it.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I asked Umar about His saying: (Repent to Allah with sincere repentance). He said: It is the servant who repents from a sin and then never returns to it, ever.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: Sincere repentance is that one repents from a sin and does not revert to it.

Ibn Humayd narrated it to us again, saying: He told me about Umar with this chain, and said: Sincere repentance is that one who commits a sin and then does not wish to return to it.

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud), regarding ﴿sincere repentance﴾, he said: He repents and then does not return.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, who said: Sincere repentance is a man who commits a sin and then does not return to it.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance﴾: that its doer does not return to that sin from which he repents. It is also said: his repentance is that he does not return to a sin he has abandoned.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿sincere repentance﴾, he said: They seek forgiveness and then do not return.

Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿sincere repentance﴾, he said: Nasuh: that you turn away from the sin and never return to it, ever.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada (O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance), he said: It is the truthful, sincere one.

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Repent to Allah with sincere repentance﴾: Sincere repentance is the truthful repentance, in which one knows that it is a true regret for his error and a love of returning to His obedience; this is the nasuh.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of the regions recited it ﴿nasuhan﴾ with a fatha on the nun, as a description (na't) and attribute (sifa) of repentance, while it is reported from Asim that he recited it ﴿nusuhan﴾ with a damma on the nun, meaning as a verbal noun (masdar) from their saying: nasaha fulan li-fulan nusuhan.

The more correct of the two recitations is the recitation of the one who reads it with a fatha on the nun, as an adjective of repentance, due to the consensus of the authorities (ijma' al-hujja) on that.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds﴾

It means: Perhaps your Lord, O believers, will erase the evil of your deeds that have passed from you. ﴿And admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning: and that He will admit you into orchards beneath whose trees rivers flow. ﴿On the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet﴾, Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them﴾, meaning: their light will go ahead of them. ﴿And on their right﴾, meaning: and on their right, their book.

As narrated:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿On the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿and on their right﴾: they take their book, in which is glad tidings. ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us"﴾: He, mighty and majestic, says, informing of the speech of the believers on the Day of Resurrection: they say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light"; they ask their Lord to let their light remain for them, so that it is not extinguished until they cross the Sirat, and that is when the hypocrite men and women will say to those who believed, ﴿Wait for us that we may acquire from your light﴾.

And in accordance with what we have said concerning that, the people of interpretation have said:

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Our Lord, perfect for us our light﴾, he said: It is the saying of the believers when the light of the hypocrites is extinguished.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Asim, from al-Hasan, who said: No one fails to be given light on the Day of Resurrection; the believer and the hypocrite are both given light, then the light of the hypocrite is extinguished, and the believer fears that his light will be extinguished; that is His saying: ﴿Our Lord, perfect for us our light﴾.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Yazid ibn Shajara, who said: He used to remind us and weep, and his deeds confirmed his words. He would say: O people, you are written with Allah, mighty and majestic, by your names and your marks, your gatherings and your secret conversations and your relations. When the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: O so-and-so son of so-and-so, take your light; and O so-and-so son of so-and-so, you have no light.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And forgive us﴾

It means: conceal our sins and do not disgrace us with them by punishing us for them. ﴿Indeed, You are over all things competent﴾, meaning: indeed, You are capable of perfecting our light for us, forgiving our sins, and other things besides.

O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination." (Qur'an 66:9)

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: "O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination."

He, mighty and majestic is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers" with the sword, "and the hypocrites" with threat and speech.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites." He said: God commanded His Prophet, upon him be prayers and peace, to strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and to be stern with the hypocrites with the legal penalties. "And be stern with them" means: be harsh with them concerning the matter of God. "Their refuge is Hell" means: their abode is Hell, and their final place to which they return is the Fire of Hell. "And wretched is the destination" he said: and wretched is the place to which they return, Hell.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 66, verse 10:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Allah sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, so the two men could avail them nothing against Allah, and it will be said: "Enter the Fire along with those who enter."﴾ (66:10)

His saying, may He be remembered, means: Allah sets forth an example for those among mankind and the rest of creation who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our servants, Noah and Lot, but they betrayed them.

It has been mentioned that the betrayal of Noah's wife toward her husband was that she was a disbeliever, and she used to tell the people that he was mad. And the betrayal of Lot's wife was that Lot used to conceal his guests, and she would point them out to others.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'isha, from Salman ibn Qays, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿but they betrayed them﴾: Noah's wife used to tell the people that he was mad, and Lot's wife used to point out the guests.

- Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Umar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'isha, from Salman ibn Qays, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say concerning this verse: As for Noah's wife, she would report that he was mad; and as for the betrayal of Lot's wife, she would point out Lot.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu 'Amir al-Hamdani, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿were under two of Our righteous servants﴾, he said: No wife of a prophet ever committed adultery. ﴿but they betrayed them﴾, he said: in religion they betrayed them.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Allah sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them﴾, he said: Their betrayal was that they were upon other than their religion. Noah's wife would inform on Noah's secret, so when anyone believed with Noah, she would inform the tyrants of Noah's people about him; that was her conduct. As for Lot's wife, whenever anyone was a guest of Lot, she would inform the people of the city who did evil about him. ﴿so the two men could avail them nothing against Allah﴾.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi Sa'id, that he heard 'Ikrimah say regarding this verse ﴿but they betrayed them﴾: in religion.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them﴾, he said: Their betrayal was that they were polytheists.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿but they betrayed them﴾, he said: They were opposing the religion of the Prophet (ﷺ), disbelievers in Allah.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Abu Mu'awiya al-Bajali, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr: What was the betrayal of Lot's wife and Noah's wife? He said: As for Lot's wife, she used to point out the guests; as for Noah's wife, I have no knowledge of her.

* *

As for His saying ﴿so the two men could avail them nothing against Allah﴾:

He says: Noah and Lot did not avail their wives against Allah when He punished them for betraying their husbands; and being prophets did not benefit them.

The interpreters have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Allah sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾ ... the verse: These two were the wives of the Prophet of Allah; when they disobeyed their Lord, their husbands could avail them nothing against Allah.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Allah sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾ ... the verse, he said: Allah says: The righteousness of these two did not avail those two at all, and the wife of Pharaoh was not harmed by Pharaoh's disbelief.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and it will be said: "Enter the Fire along with those who enter"﴾:

Allah will say to them on the Day of Resurrection: Enter, O two women, the Fire of Hell along with those who enter it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 66, verse 11:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said: "My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people."﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: And Allah set forth an example for those who affirmed Allah and declared Him one: the wife of Pharaoh, who believed in Allah and declared Him one, and affirmed His Messenger Moses, while she was under the authority of an enemy of Allah, a disbeliever. The disbelief of her husband did not harm her, since she was a believer in Allah, and it was part of Allah's decree concerning His creation that "no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another" and that "for every soul is what it has earned." When she said: ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾, Allah answered her and built for her a house in Paradise.

As evidence:

⁕ Ismail ibn Hafs al-Ablī [with a hamza, then a b with two vowels, attributing him to al-Ubulla] narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman, from Salman, who said: The wife of Pharaoh was being tortured by the sun. When he left her, the angels would shade her with their wings, and she would see her house in Paradise.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman, who said: Sulayman said: The wife of Pharaoh... and he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastawa'i, who said: al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah narrated to us, who said: The wife of Pharaoh used to ask who had prevailed, and it would be said: Moses and Aaron prevailed. She would say: I believe in the Lord of Moses and Aaron. So Pharaoh sent for her and said: "Look for the greatest rock you can find; if she persists in her statement, throw it upon her, and if she recants, she is his wife." When they came to her, she raised her eyes to the sky and saw her house in the sky, so she persisted in her statement, and Allah took her soul, and the rock was thrown upon a body in which there was no spirit.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾, and he was the most insolent of the people of the earth toward Allah and the most distant from Allah. By Allah, the disbelief of her husband did not harm her when she obeyed her Lord, so that you may know that Allah is a just judge who does not punish His servant except for his own sin.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds﴾

She says: Deliver me from the punishment of Pharaoh, and from my becoming one who does his deeds, and that is his disbelief in Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And save me from the wrongdoing people﴾

She says: Purify me and rescue me from the deeds of the people who disbelieve in You, and from their punishment.

**The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted:** ﴿And Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit, and she affirmed the words of her Lord and His Scriptures, and she was among the devout.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And God sets forth an example for those who believe﴾ ﴿and Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity﴾, meaning: she who kept Gabriel, peace be upon him, away from the opening of her garment's collar. Every tear or split in a garment is called *farj* (an opening), and likewise every crack or fissure in a wall, or an opening in a roof, is a *farj*.

And His saying: ﴿so We breathed into her of Our Spirit﴾

It means: We breathed into her, into the collar of her garment, which is her *farj*, of Our Spirit, that is, of Gabriel, who is the Spirit.

The people of *ta'wil* (the exegetes) have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said so:

It was related to us by Ibn 'Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿so We breathed into her of Our Spirit﴾: "We breathed into her collar of Our Spirit." ﴿and she affirmed the words of her Lord﴾: "She believed in 'Isa, who is the Word of God." ﴿and His Scriptures﴾: "meaning the Torah and the Gospel." ﴿and she was among the devout﴾: "and she was among the obedient people."

Similarly:

It was related to us by Ibn 'Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿among the devout﴾: "among the obedient."

End of the tafsir of Surat al-Tahrim.
